description: MAIT University DBMS practical formatting style. Academic, concise, bullet-oriented theory with proper SQL formatting.

rules: Start with a clear 2-3 line definition of the concept
Follow with numbered bullet points for key concepts (1. 2. 3. ...)
Include characteristics or properties section where relevant
Include applications section where relevant
Keep each bullet point 1-2 lines maximum
Use academic concise language throughout
No ChatGPT-style long paragraphs
No motivational or explanatory filler
Format similar to DDL/Constraints/Joins style from MAIT PDF
Total theory length: 120-200 words
Write SQL keywords in UPPERCASE (SELECT, FROM, WHERE, CREATE, INSERT, etc.)
Include CREATE TABLE with appropriate schema if needed for the experiment
Include INSERT INTO statements with realistic sample data
Show the actual SQL queries demonstrating the experiment topic
Use MariaDB/MySQL compatible syntax
Do NOT include comments in the code
Keep all SQL in a single code block
Use proper indentation for readability
Use DELIMITER for procedures/functions/triggers
Show output as it would appear in a MariaDB/MySQL terminal
Include the MariaDB prompt style where appropriate
Show query results in tabular format
Keep output realistic and matching the source code queries
Include 'Query OK' and 'rows affected' messages where appropriate
Questions 1-3: Basic conceptual questions about the experiment topic
Questions 4-5: Intermediate application-based questions
Question 6: Technical or tricky question that tests deeper understanding
All questions must relate to the specific SQL concepts in the experiment
Answers should be concise (2-3 sentences max)
Style: university viva examination format

formatting.aim_style: 1-2 line clear statement starting with 'To study and implement'
formatting.font_hierarchy: Title > Section Heading > Body > Bullet > Code
